The first time my phone offered to connect to a satellite, I thought we had finally figured it out. Internet from space. Everywhere.

No more dead zones, terrible airplane WiFi, or getting stranded somewhere without a signal.

Except… satellite internet has been around for decades. And for most of that time, it was painfully slow, ridiculously expensive, and nowhere near good enough to replace regular internet.

So what actually changed?

Caya went down the rabbit hole of satellite internet, starting with Boeing's failed attempt to bring broadband to airplanes in 2004, and ending with Starlink's thousands of satellites orbiting Earth today.

title: The impossible science of Space Internet
